names.name: Bavarian cream
names.said: Ask whether it is custard or whipped. The answer tells you what kind of shop you are in.

text.what: A raised round with no hole, filled with a set custard — Bavarian cream is custard lightened with whipped cream and held with gelatin — and finished in sugar, or iced with chocolate, at which point most counters call it a Boston cream.
text.story: The filled fried round is the older European form; the American shop split it by filling. Jam is a jelly donut or a bismarck; pastry cream and its relatives are custard, Bavarian or Boston cream depending on the shop and the region. The words are not standard and no authority governs them.
text.how: Fry the round, cool it, then inject from the side with a nozzle until it gains weight in the hand. Chocolate icing goes on the top face after.
text.today: The filled donuts are the ones a shop fills in the morning and the ones left over at closing, because a filled donut does not hold overnight the way a glazed ring does.

kin.as: Same shell, jam instead of custard.
The nozzle, and the weight in the hand.
